subject: Urgent: Production throttling during batch inference (rate/quota/burst)
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintext.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@fintext.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate / timeouts during overnight batch - urgent

Rishi,

We saw a major spike overnight during our scheduled batch scoring window (02:00 - 04:00 PST). Latency shot up to 2.1s/token and we began seeing a surge of 429 / rate_limit_exceeded errors after the first hour. Throughput dropped by ~60% and the whole pipeline started retrying, which in turn amplified the request rate and made things worse.

Attached are the first-pass logs and our job schedule. This is on the Dedicated capacity pool you provisioned under our account. Our SRE team is seeing repeated 429s that didn't happen before the config changes last week. Can you triage and escalate? This is impacting SLAs for multiple customers.

Attachments: support_logs_2026-10-29.txt (text)

Thanks,
Samir Shah
CPO, FinText
samir.shah@fintext.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintext.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate / timeouts during overnight batch - urgent

Samir —

Thanks for the quick heads up and for the logs. I'm escalating immediately to our infra/support leads (cc'd). Preliminary ask: can you confirm whether the jobs are hitting a single route/model endpoint repeatedly or if they are spread across multiple models? That will help us narrow whether this is per-model rate limiting or an org-level burst/quota config.

Short-term steps from our side:
- Monica will pull recent quota/burst policy snapshots for your org and check for recent changes.
- Markus will review serving metrics for the Dedicated pool and surface any throttling or kernel-level stalls.
- We'll provide an emergency mitigation plan (temporary override + traffic shaping) within 2 hours.

I will also reach out to my manager Laura for executive visibility. We're treating this as a Sev 2 until you confirm customer impact.

Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintext.ai>, Priya Rao <priya@fintext.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate / timeouts during overnight batch - urgent

Quick diagnostic — pulled the last two burst policy snapshots and traffic histograms for FinText. Findings:

- There was a policy change pushed on 2026-10-27 at 23:48 PDT that reduced org-level burst_capacity from 20k tokens to 2k tokens and simultaneously lowered per-minute quota. The change was flagged as a cost-control toggle but the delta is larger than intended.
- The client's batch jobs are very spiky by design (short, dense bursts). With the new burst_capacity they exceed the allowed instantaneous window, so requests are being token-throttled and returning 429. Retries from the client amplify the observed request rate, causing a feedback loop.
- Serving metrics show sustained scheduler backpressure in the dedicated pool between 02:15-03:30 PDT with queue spikes and longer kernel queue times (see attached snapshot).

Immediate mitigation options (pick one):
1) Apply a temporary override to restore previous burst_capacity (to 20k) + per-minute quota for the FinText org (recommended) — this is low-risk and reversible.
2) Apply per-route rate-limiting on the most aggressive jobs to smooth traffic, but this requires coordination on the FinText side and will introduce throttling per job.
3) If you prefer no config changes, we can implement an emergency traffic-shaper proxy on the Dedicated pool for the next 48 hours.

If you give us the green light I'll implement option (1) and monitor for stabilization, and we can follow with a recommended long-term policy (rule tuning and burst window resizing).

Attachments: burst_policy_snapshot.png

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintext.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@fintext.ai>, FinText DevOps <ops@fintext.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate / timeouts during overnight batch - urgent

Thanks Monica — this looks exactly like the right diagnosis. We rolled the cost-control toggle because of a budget alarm but we didn't anticipate that the burst window change would have this side-effect for our dense jobs.

Given the impact, we want option (1) — please restore the previous burst_capacity and per-minute quota immediately and let us know when it's in place. We've also paused retries on our side to avoid amplifying the problem.

To be transparent, I've looped in our CEO and ProcOps (copying Priya) because this caused an SLA breach for our enterprise tier. We will expect a short incident summary and next steps.

Samir
CPO, FinText

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintext.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec update and mitigation plan — FinText throttling incident

Samir —

First, apologies for the SLA impact. We own this and are treating it with exec priority. Summary of what we observed and actions taken so far: 

- Root cause: unintended cost-control change that reduced burst_capacity and per-minute quota for your org; caused token-level throttling for your high-density batch jobs.
- Immediate action: we applied a temporary override at 2026-11-02T09:00:00 PST to restore the previous burst_capacity and quota for FinText (Monica executed). Initial telemetry shows error rate dropped from ~18% to <1% and latency stabilized.
- Next steps (24–72h):
  - We'll run a joint post-mortem to tighten guardrails around cost-control toggles and to add an approval flow for changes that impact burst windows.
  - Our infra team will propose a tuned long-term policy that preserves cost controls but recognizes bursty workloads (scheduled review by 2026-11-04).
  - We'll provide a formal incident report and credit proposal for the SLA breach by 2026-11-05.

Markus and I are available for a 30-minute incident review with FinText leadership today at 15:00 PST if that works for you. Rishi will coordinate.

Best,
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@fintext.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exec update and mitigation plan — FinText throttling incident

Samir —

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Confirming we applied the override and monitored the 02:00 batch window — telemetry looks stable. Attached is the proposed override patch (diff) and a short set of tuning recommendations we will push after the PM/ops review.

Action items I own:
- Schedule post-mortem with FinText ops and our infra on 2026-11-04 10:00 PST.
- Deliver incident report and credit proposal by 2026-11-05 (Laura and I).
- Implement conservative guardrails on cost-control toggles by 2026-11-09 (Monica + Markus).

If you want, Monica can keep an elevated monitoring window for another 48 hours.

Attachments: proposed_override_patch.diff

Thanks — we'll follow up with the incident report.

Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
summary: Customer FinText experienced high latency and 429 throttling during batch jobs after a cost-control change reduced burst_capacity and per-minute quota. Redwood applied a temporary override to restore burst capacity, stabilized telemetry, and committed to a post-mortem, policy guardrails, and an incident report with credits.
